episodes.204491: A traditional monsoon flow on the western flank of an upper level high over the central U.S. combined with daytime heating resulted in the development of shower and thunderstorm activity across the higher terrain during the early through late afternoon hours. Some of this shower and thunderstorm activity moved over the South Fork burn scar on both August 17th and August 18th resulting in flash flooding and debris flow across roadways on and downstream of the burn scar. Overall impacts were reported to be more severe and widespread on August 17th compared to August 18th. Finally, a brief landspout was observed in Las Vegas during the mid afternoon on August 18th as well as near the Bernalillo and Sandoval County line during the mid afternoon on August 19th.
episodes.204556: On the 19th, South Texas remained under the influence of a weak surface ridging. However, the main 500 mb high ridge that had been a fixture over the area continued to shift further westward across the SW CONUS. This westward shift allowed for a more favorable environment for lift and precipitation with a passage of a series of shortwave troughs expected this day. With the combination of mid to upper-level forcing from the shortwaves, daytime heating, and ample moisture, thunderstorm activity was anticipated to increase in intensity and coverage through the day. A series of stronger storms led to gusty winds, particularly across our marine areas.
episodes.204579: Hot weather resulted in daily episodes of clusters of storms with damaging winds, isolated hail, and some areas of flash flooding from August 12 through August 18th.  The most widespread activity occurred August 15th, and 18th, when several lines of storms moved through the area.
episodes.204581: Numerous thunderstorms and heavy rain ahead of a slow moving cold front caused some flooding in southern Rock and Walworth Counties.
episodes.204603: Marginally hot and rather humid conditions on the 19th produced adequate instability for scattered afternoon thunderstorms ahead of an approaching cold front.  Thicker cloud cover to the north of Interstate 70 produced a differential heating boundary that storms formed along, with one of the day's first cells producing isolated wind damage in Shelby County.
episodes.204614: During the early morning hours of August 19th, a complex of storms brought severe winds to portions of Johnson County, KS. A cloud to ground lightning strike also caused a large house fire.
episodes.204615: During the early morning hours of August 19th, a complex of storms brought severe wind gusts due to a microburst to portions of western Jackson County.
episodes.204638: During the morning and afternoon, widely scattered storms developed across portions of east central and northeast Kansas. Several downburst winds occurred, resulting in several downed trees, power lines, and small structures.
episodes.204713: A thunderstorm in Lawrence County during the evening of August 19, 2025, was the cause of a person being struck by lightning near Ethridge.
episodes.204787: Differential heating and upslope flow led to the development of thunderstorms during the afternoon of the 18th. One of these thunderstorms produced a microburst between Pecos and Mentone.
episodes.204799: A cold front dropping southeast towards the Lower Ohio Valley produced a broken line of convection. While convection along the line was in Orange County, it produced a measured severe wind gust.
episodes.204800: A cold front dropping southeast towards the Lower Ohio Valley produced a broken line of convection. While convection along the line moved through Jefferson County, it blew a tree down.
episodes.205017: Scattered thunderstorms developed along and ahead of a cold front during the early afternoon of August 19th. Convection existed in a high instability and low shear environment, so damaging winds were the primary threat for the day. One thunderstorm did produce isolated wind damage in northeast Reynolds County.
episodes.205175: An isolated severe storm over Apalachee bay produced a measured wind gust of 55 knots.  In addition, a waterspout was reported offshore of Saint George Island.
episodes.205194: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed across portions of northwestern Arkansas during the afternoon and evening of the 19th, as a frontal boundary moved into the area. Very unstable air combined with weak wind shear resulted in intense but relatively short-lived thunderstorms, the strongest of which produced damaging outflow wind and large hail up to quarter size.
episodes.205196: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed across portions of eastern Oklahoma during the afternoon and evening of the 19th, as a frontal boundary moved into the area. Very unstable air combined with weak wind shear resulted in intense but relatively short-lived thunderstorms, the strongest of which produced damaging outflow wind.
episodes.205223: With hot temperatures in place, afternoon pop up thunderstorms lead to isolated microbursts across central and portions of northern Arkansas.
episodes.205350: Marine thunderstorms produced strong wind gusts.
episodes.205354: Thunderstorms produced hail and damaging winds across portions of SE Texas.
episodes.205365: Scattered thunderstorms developed during the afternoon hours in a humid airmass.

episodes.205501: A severe thunderstorm brought severe wind gusts to northern Wilkin County in west central Minnesota during the evening hours.
episodes.205593: A wet August resulted in renewed minor to locally moderate river flooding along portions of the middle Big Sioux River.
episodes.205704: Two separate clusters of thunderstorms moved across portions of central and south-central Kansas during the afternoon hours of August 19. These storms produced multiple reports of large hail up to half dollar size and wind gusts up to 72 mph.
episodes.206082: Scattered storms developed west to east across the area leading to wind damage in Thomas and Logan counties including to a residence in Thomas county. Wind gusts of 60 and 64 mph were recorded at the Goodland Airport as well. A 68 mph wind gust was recorded 9 WSW Winona.
episodes.206142: Diurnal multi-cell thunderstorms produced observations of severe winds and wind damage across northern Oklahoma on the 18th.
episodes.206143: Numerous strong to severe thunderstorms developed across much of Oklahoma during the afternoon and evening of the 19th. With steep temperature lapse rates, strong instability and weak wind shear, multiple damage-producing downburst wind events occurred across the WFO Norman Forecast Area.
episodes.206401: During the afternoon and evening of the 18th, a few rounds of thunderstorms brought torrential rainfall to much of northern Illinois resulting in flash flooding. One particularly strong storm also produced damaging winds in DeKalb County. Initial reports estimate $8.8 million in flood damages around northern and northeast Illinois, and around $2.5 million in the city of Chicago alone.
episodes.206531: A cold front triggered scattered strong to severe thunderstorms in the Illinois River Valley during the evening of August 18th.  A few of the cells produced 60-70mph wind gusts and minor wind damage, as well as prolific lightning.
episodes.206532: A cluster of thunderstorms intensified over Logan and Macon counties during the pre-dawn hours of August 19th.  One of the cells produced a downburst with 80-100 mph winds and significant wind damage in the town of Maroa in Macon County.  Strong 70-80 mph winds also caused damage further south in Forsyth on the north side of Decatur.
episodes.206533: A broken line of thunderstorms formed ahead of a cold front along the I-70 corridor during the afternoon of August 19th.  One of the cells produced 50-60 mph wind gusts and isolated wind damage in Lawrence County.
episodes.206581: Heavy rainfall during the middle of August resulted in minor flooding along portions of the  Trempealeau and Platte rivers in Western Wisconsin.
episodes.206584: Heavy rain throughout the middle of August contributed to rises along many area rivers in northeast Iowa. This included minor to moderate flooding along portions of the Little Cedar and Cedar Rivers, as well as the Upper Iowa and Turkey Rivers.
episodes.206621: Hurricane Erin dominated the upper-level pattern and steered the remnants of an MCS directly towards the Mid-South. Shower and thunderstorm coverage was much higher than in previous days as storms tapped into moderate to high instability. Storms were able to quickly grow upscale and produce damaging winds and some sub-severe hail. Several outflow boundaries were produced from convective coverage with measured 40-50 mph winds associated with the boundaries. These winds were enough to produce sporadic damage in addition to stronger winds from severe thunderstorms.

episodes.206676: A cold front sagged through the Quad State from north to south later in the day on the 19th. A jagged line of thunderstorms developed during the afternoon across Southeast Missouri and Southern Illinois, dipping southward through mid afternoon. MLCAPE maxed out early afternoon around 3000-3500J/kg with DCAPE of 1200J/kg. Effective shear was limited, below 30kts. In Southern Illinois, the lone damage report was a tree blown down in Hardin County.
episodes.206677: A cold front sagged through the Quad State from north to south later in the day on the 19th. A jagged line of thunderstorms developed during the afternoon across Southeast Missouri and Southern Illinois, progressing southward and crossing Western Kentucky late afternoon. MLCAPE maxed out early afternoon around 3000-3500J/kg with DCAPE of 1200J/kg. Effective shear was limited, below 30kts. The lone damage report in Western Kentucky was downburst winds blowing down multiple trees in West Viola.
episodes.206678: A cold front sagged through the Quad State from north to south later in the day on the 19th. A jagged line of thunderstorms developed during the afternoon across Southeast Missouri and Southern Illinois, dipping southward through late afternoon. MLCAPE maxed out early afternoon around 3000-3500J/kg with DCAPE of 1200J/kg. Effective shear was limited, below 30kts. Wind damage, mainly to trees, was most widespread in Cape Girardeau County as a storm tracked southeastward through the county during the early afternoon. Wind damage was also reported in Butler County with hail noted in Carter County.
episodes.206718: Isolated strong to severe thunderstorms developed across parts of Northern Louisiana during the afternoon on August 18th. These thunderstorms formed within an environment with slightly more favorable mid-level lapse rates of around 7 C/km and hot temperatures near 100 degrees. Weak deep layer shear of 10 knots or less limited storm organization, but despite the unorganized nature of the convection, very strong heating and instability supported strong to marginally severe thunderstorms capable of isolated microbursts and wind damage. As a result, a few instances of damaging wind gusts were reported across parts of Northern Louisiana.
episodes.206736: An upper high right over southern New Mexico trapped low level monsoonal moisture under it.  Overnight and afternoon thunderstorms were slow moving and heavy rain caused flash flooding near Rincon and La Union.
episodes.206737: An upper high right over the El Paso area trapped low level monsoonal moisture under it. Early evening thunderstorms were slow moving and heavy rain caused flash flooding near Canutillo.
episodes.206738: An upper high over western New Mexico trapped low level monsoonal moisture over the Rio Grande Valley.  Afternoon thunderstorms brought heavy rain areas of west El Paso with flooding reported near Redd Road and Doniphan.
episodes.206788: Isolated strong to severe thunderstorms developed near a surface frontal boundary and a decaying MCV across central and western Arkansas in the early afternoon on August 19th. Farther southwest, convection was slower to develop but increased in coverage through the afternoon. Shear was quite weak as were mid-level lapse rates. However, a very moist air mass fueled 2000-3000 J/kg MLCAPE. With surface temperatures in the upper 90s to near 100 degrees, steep low-level lapse rates allowed for efficient microburst production with the stronger storm cores. As a result, an isolated severe thunderstorm produced damaging wind gusts and small hail in northern Howard County.
episodes.206832: A retreating mid to upper-level high allowed convection to develop with strong daytime heating in a moist airmass. Some of these storms produced damaging wind gusts and one tornado.
episodes.206876: Afternoon sea breeze thunderstorms produce a strong wind gust over the Tampa Bay waters.
episodes.207093: Moisture and instability pooled along a nearly stationary frontal boundary across southeast Virginia on August 18. Slow-moving showers and storms trained over the lower Virginia Peninsula region, with flash flooding occurring in the late afternoon and evenings hours.
episodes.207094: A weak trough aloft and weak surface low were located in the vicinity of southeast Virginia on August 19. Moist, easterly flow led to widespread showers with localized higher rainfall rates; the slow-moving showers on the Virginia Eastern Shore produced areas of flash flooding in the morning hours.
episodes.207132: A series of strong thunderstorms brought torrential rain and flooding to portions of far northwestern Indiana during the evening and night of the 18th. Automated rain gauges and Cocorahs reports from northern Lake and Porter Counties generally ranged between two and four inches with isolated reports closer to five inches. Initial estimates have around 1,000 structures flooded in Lake County amounting to near $4 million in damages.
episodes.207133: Thunderstorms produced strong winds and heavy rainfall over southern Lake Michigan during the evening of the 18th. The Michigan City C-MAN station recorded a 52 mph gust as storms were moving in.
episodes.207143: As a low pressure system moved into central Kansas, storms developed and created an outflow boundary. This boundary moved into Barber county rapidly initiating convection which produced a severe wind gust report before exiting south out of Kansas.
episodes.207160: The combination of strong instability and strong wind shear resulted in scattered severe thunderstorms across portions of the Concho Valley and Northern Edwards Plateau on the afternoon of the 19th. A few severe storms also occurred on the 17th. The storms produced damaging winds.
episodes.207669: A small area of thunderstorms formed in Mitchell and Jewell counties during the mid afternoon hours. One storm produced quarter size hail near Glen Elder. The storms formed along weak boundaries in the region with moderate instability of 3,000-4,000 surface based CAPE and as a weak upper wave rotated south from Nebraska around upper level high pressure over the Four Corners region.

events.narrative: Downed tree and branches reported.

Numerous reports of street, yard, and basement flooding came out of the Joliet, Crest Hill, Lockport, and Homer Glen areas. In Homer Glen, a video shared via social media showed 1 to 2 feet of standing water on a residential street southwest of 167th St and Cedar Rd. Around 50 flooded structures were estimated amounting to roughly $250,000 in damages.

Extensive flash flooding was reported around southern Cook County. Numerous reports of street and basement flooding came out of Orland Hills, Midlothian, Homer Glen, and Tinley Park. At least one foot of water was reported along 183rd and 179th streets near LaGrange Rd. In Orland Park, 143rd St near Creek Crossing Dr was closed due to flooding. Wolf Rd was flooded near 167th St near the Marley Creek crossing in Homer Glen. One Cocorahs observer in Midlothian recorded 5.7 of 24-hour rainfall the next morning with several other reports in the area between 3 and 4. Damage estimates around the area come in at $1.5 million with roughly 300 structures flooded.

Numerous reports of street flooding came out of the east side of Mokena, south of I-80. Near the Hickory Creek train station, at least 6 inches of water were flooding a viaduct. Up to 3 feet of water were reported on a roadway near Hercht Park. A nearby private weather station recorded 3.62 inches of rain from approximately 6 to 9 PM CST. Reports show flooding began in the area following an initial push of heavy rain during the 6PM CST hour, with additional flooding following subsequent storms through the evening. An estimated 200 structures were flooded around the Mokena, Frankfort, and Crete areas totaling around $1 million in flood damages.

An estimated 700 structures were flooded in southeast Cook County, including Dolton, Harvey, South Holland, and Thornton. Two lanes of I-294 near the quarry in Thornton were covered in water. Damages in the area are estimated at around $3.5 million.
Multiple reports of cars stalled around Beloit as they drove into flooded roads.
